claim: Damages for personal injuries received as a result of a road traffic accident
requested_remedy: Damages for personal injuries received as a result of a road traffic accident
parties: Defendant: The Second Defendant (name not specified), The First Defendant (name not specified), The Third Defendant (name not specified)

facts.F1: The Plaintiff was involved in a road traffic accident on 23rd January, 1967, when a van driven by the First Defendant collided with her car.
facts.F2: The van in question is alleged to be owned by the Second Defendant.
facts.F3: The Plaintiff received severe injuries, including a severe sprain of the neck, whiplash, and arthritic changes, which have resulted in ongoing pain and suffering.
facts.F4: After the accident, the Plaintiff saw Dr. Peter Wu and Dr. Yau, an orthopaedic surgeon, and underwent treatment, including neck traction and hospitalization.
facts.F5: The Plaintiff was unable to work for several months and has experienced ongoing symptoms, including pain, dizziness, and disturbed vision.
facts.F6: Dr. Yau recommended that the Plaintiff undergo a spinal fusion operation to correct the instability between cervical 4 and 5 vertebrae.
facts.F7: The Plaintiff is a physiotherapist employed by the Hong Kong Government, with a monthly salary of $2,500, and has been unable to play golf and tennis or participate in social activities due to her injuries.
facts.F8: Special damages amount to $2,933.32, including $2,615.32 for loss of wages, $273 for hospital expenses, and $45 damage to the Plaintiff's car.
facts.F9: The Plaintiff experienced ongoing pain and suffering, loss of amenities, and loss of future earnings.
facts.F10: The Plaintiff is recommended to undergo a major operation as per Dr. Yau's recommendation.

facts.F1: The Plaintiff was employed by the 1st Defendant as a demolition worker.
facts.F2: On 31 January 1982, the 1st Defendant fell through a hole in the upper floor and landed on the Plaintiff's head, causing a Jefferson fracture (broken neck).
facts.F3: The Plaintiff was 57 years old at the time of the accident and turned 63 in April 1988.
facts.F4: The Plaintiff has always worked in laboring jobs, first as a mason and then as a demolition worker.
facts.F5: The Plaintiff is married with two children, a married daughter and a 14-year-old son, and has been unable to send them money since the accident.
facts.F6: The Plaintiff was admitted to Kwong Wah Hospital for 75 days, with 53 days in traction, and later had cramps and numbness in his hands and forearms.
facts.F7: The Plaintiff was offered major surgery to fuse the base of the skull to the cervical spine but refused.
facts.F8: The Plaintiff has permanent disabilities, including pain over his neck and shoulder, limitation of neck movements, intermittent numbness of his arms and hands, and weakness of his right hand and both lower limbs.
facts.F9: The Plaintiff is now only fit for a job such as a watchman, liftman, or caretaker.
facts.F10: Dr. Wedderburn and Dr. Ng Shi Hon agreed that the Plaintiff should not have the surgery offered.
facts.F11: Dr. Ng estimated the Plaintiff's loss of earning capacity at 20% of the whole man.
facts.F12: Dr. Mao assessed the Plaintiff's impairment at 14% of the whole man.
facts.F13: The Plaintiff's age, health, and disability were considered in determining the multiplier for future loss of earnings.

claim: damages for personal injuries sustained in a fall from height at work
requested_remedy: damages for personal injuries sustained in a fall from height at work

facts.F1: The Plaintiff (CHAN KWOK WAI) was a painter employed by the Electrical and Mechanic Services Department (EMSD) at the time of the accident.
facts.F2: The accident occurred on 10 February 2004, when the Plaintiff and his colleagues were assigned to paint a transmission tower situated on Kau Yi Chau, a remote island of Hong Kong.
facts.F3: The tower was a lattice structure with four vertical columns interconnected by diagonal struts, and six levels of platforms, each about 15 ft. high.
facts.F4: The Plaintiff was supplied with personal protective equipment, including an upper chest harness, a lower pelvic harness, an independent lifeline, a 31 in. lanyard, a 9 in. lanyard, a figure-of-eight ring, and a number of carabineer hooks.
facts.F5: The Plaintiff's personal protective equipment provided two fall prevention systems: a movable anchorage on the independent lifeline, and a fixed anchorage on the tower structure.
facts.F6: At the time of the accident, the Plaintiff was on level 5 of the tower, attempting to paint the outside of the tower.
facts.F7: The Plaintiff detached the long lanyard from the tower structure, stepped up, and straddled on the lower rung of the guardrails to try to reach for the ring on the lifeline.
facts.F8: During this manoeuvre, the wind became gusty, and the Plaintiff lost balance and fell approximately 20 m to the ground.
facts.F9: The Plaintiff suffered severe injuries, including fractures at L-1 vertebra, pelvis, right ankle, and both calcaneus (heels).
facts.F10: The Plaintiff used the personal protection equipment improperly.
facts.F11: A monsoon signal was in effect on the day of the accident.
facts.F12: There were gusty winds on the day of the accident.

facts.F1: The deceased, Lam Sze Ching, was the sole proprietor of the Maintain Ease (Hong Kong) Company, a cleaning company.
facts.F2: In the early hours of the morning of 24 October 1994, the deceased was performing cleaning works for the Hang Seng Bank Ltd at the external wall of the Hang Seng Bank Building in Connaught Road Central.
facts.F3: The deceased had hired a special purpose truck with a folding crane from the 1st defendant, Proficiency Industrial Products Limited, for the cleaning works.
facts.F4: The 2nd defendant, Ip Kwai Ming, was employed by the 1st defendant to drive the truck and operate the crane.
facts.F5: At about 5:15 am, a double decker bus owned by the 3rd defendant, China Motor Bus Company Limited, and driven by its employee, the 4th defendant, Lam Kwok Ming, hit the jib cabin, throwing the deceased and the 2nd defendant onto the ground.
facts.F6: The deceased died later the same morning from the injuries he received as a result of the fall.
facts.F7: There was no dispute that the truck was parked on the pavement with its crane extended over the second lane of the westbound carriageway of Connaught Road Central without any hazard lights on, and no part of Connaught Road Central was closed or blocked off by cones or warning lights.
facts.F8: The road was not closed off by cones or warning lights when the accident occurred.
facts.F9: The deceased had suggested not blocking off the road as part of the cleaning works.
facts.F10: The deceased did not ensure that the necessary safety precautions were taken during the cleaning works
facts.F11: The deceased earned an income and had expenses that were considered when calculating damages.
facts.F12: The parties agreed on a multiplier for damages calculation.

facts.F4: Ms Ng claims she was required to lift the heavy bags, one at a time, with both hands in front of her, and then walk down the staircase carrying the bag.
facts.F5: Ms Lau, a coworker of Ms Ng, claims they rolled the bags down the staircase to avoid having to lift them.
facts.F6: The staircase had damaged tiles that were not covered or repaired by the Golf Club.
facts.F7: Ms Ng was taken to an Accident and Emergency Department and treated conservatively with physiotherapy, bed rest, and analgesics.
facts.F8: Ms Ng suffered persistent back pain, depression, and anxiety after the accident.
facts.F9: Ms Ng was assessed for her physical and mental conditions in order to determine the extent of her injuries.

claim: claims damages for personal injuries sustained in a traffic accident
requested_remedy: claims damages for personal injuries sustained in a traffic accident
parties: Defendant: SHING WAH CHAI (1st Defendant) and SHING CHUNG LAM (2nd Defendant)

facts.F1: The accident occurred on Tuen Mun Road at 1330 hours on 8th January 1983.
facts.F2: The Plaintiff was changing the front off-side wheel of his employer's goods vehicle on the carriageway when the 1st Defendant's Suzuki goods vehicle collided with him.
facts.F3: The road surface at the place of the accident was good and dry, and the weather conditions were good.
facts.F4: The Plaintiff's vehicle had a puncture, and he brought it to a halt in the middle lane, slightly slanting to the right.
facts.F5: The Plaintiff's van boy, FAN Chu, said that the Plaintiff's vehicle protruded a foot or so into the fast lane when it finally came to rest.
facts.F6: The Plaintiff dismounted and attempted to change the wheel, but was struck by the 1st Defendant's vehicle before he could complete the task.
facts.F7: The Plaintiff suffered fractures of 2 ribs, of the pelvis in four places, and has a ½ inch shortening of the right leg and limitation of the left hip joint movement.
facts.F8: The Plaintiff attempted the repair with the aid of his van boy, FAN Chu.
facts.F9: The Plaintiff had assumed too much responsibility for his safety to his van boy, FAN Chu.
